forward.meaning: surviving every 2-adic depth == the forward orbit of M never exceeds M
forward.verdict: a large set, entirely populated by numbers that reach 1 — proves nothing about cycles

backward.meaning: surviving every 3-adic depth == an infinite backward chain bounded by M == a nontrivial cycle exists
backward.verdict: empty if and only if no nontrivial cycle exists — the same problem, restated

proved: Cycle.toBackChain — a cycle is a bounded backward chain
BackChain.exists_periodic — any bounded chain forces a periodic point <= M
BackChain.ne_one — for q=1, M>1 no element of the chain is 1
BackChain.exists_nontrivial_periodic — so that periodic point is a nontrivial cycle
lean.not_proved: Koenig's lemma: 'survives every finite depth' => 'an infinite chain exists'. Needs dependent choice.
lean.axioms: propext, Quot.sound — no sorryAx, no Classical.choice
lean.nonvacuity: q7_has_periodic_point instantiates the general theorem on the real cycle 11 -> 5 -> 11
